November 11, 2026

Scott Colom flips Mississippi Senate seat, first Black senator from the state since Reconstruction

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

CNN projected Democrat Scott Colom the winner over Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi, and Hyde-Smith conceded. Colom, 43, becomes the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Mississippi in more than 40 years and the first Black person elected to the seat since Reconstruction, 145 years ago. The race stayed undecided for more than a week while officials reviewed thousands of provisional ballots, and the result flips a Republican-held seat in a state Donald Trump carried by 22.9 points in 2024. Hyde-Smith had previously blocked Colom's nomination to a federal judgeship.

House reaches 218 signatures to force a vote on Epstein Files Transparency Act II

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

A discharge petition for the Epstein Files Transparency Act II reached the 218 signatures needed to force a floor vote, bypassing Speaker Mike Johnson. Rep. Thomas Massie, who filed the petition, said he is working with Reps. Pramila Jayapal, Teresa Leger Fernandez and Ro Khanna to bring it to the floor. The bill would let survivors and state attorneys general file federal lawsuits against the Justice Department to force the release of additional Epstein files, and would give Congress the power to demand unredacted documents. A House vote is expected this month before the measure moves to the Senate.

White House warns Congress that investigating Trump could bring criminal prosecution

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

White House counsel Will Sharpe sent a letter to Rep. Robert Garcia warning that planned congressional investigations of Donald Trump and his circle could cross into criminal conduct, according to Punchbowl News. The letter argues that congressional investigations must serve a legitimate legislative purpose, and that members could face prosecution if they do not. The warning comes as Democrats prepare to take control of House committees in January.

Nvidia board prepares to oust Jensen Huang after second affair report

tags: markets, tech
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews, @oafnation_actual

The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board is preparing to remove founder and CEO Jensen Huang, 63, and could meet as soon as Wednesday to decide his future. The report followed allegations that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, 48, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, who reports to him; five former employees described the pair being affectionate at a San Jose hotel during the company's March GTC conference, with company security detaining and offering a nondisclosure agreement to a bystander who filmed them. The allegations come days after Huang admitted in a company-wide memo to being unfaithful to his wife, following reports of an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom U.S. officials believe worked for Chinese intelligence. Nvidia shares fell as much as 8% in after-hours trading; outside counsel Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz is leading the board's investigation and the FBI is reportedly examining the relationship. China has rejected the espionage allegations.

Senate takes up permitting bill that environmental groups say guts protections

tags: climate, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Senate began voting Monday night on a permitting measure called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, with amendments expected throughout the week. Supporters say it would speed project approvals and lower energy costs, while environmental groups warn it would weaken long-standing safeguards, including limiting tribes to a one-year review window under the Clean Water Act. According to the NRDC, the bill would write Trump EPA proposals limiting state authority into law, curb EPA power to protect areas such as Alaska's Bristol Bay, and let states take over federal wildlife reviews under the Endangered Species Act. Sen. Tammy Duckworth and other Democrats are pushing for changes, arguing Congress should not rush a bill handing the president more power.

Sanders opposes Schumer as Senate Democratic leader

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews, @carolinegleich

Sen. Bernie Sanders said at a Capitol news conference that he will not support Chuck Schumer's bid to remain Senate Democratic leader, calling for a vigorous debate about the party's direction. Sen. Chris Van Hollen said he is calling fellow senators as he weighs a challenge, though Schumer has no declared opponent; Democrats are expected to choose leaders in early December and will hold at least 54 seats in January. Caroline Gleich, the 2024 Democratic Senate nominee in Utah, also called for new leadership, saying Schumer's personal political fund gave her campaign nothing while a Schumer-aligned super PAC spent over $390 million on Senate races that cycle.

Democrats post historic gains across the South and red states

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @carolinegleich

Democrats won the popular vote in the South for the first time in decades, leading Senate races in the region by nearly 8.8 points and House races by 3.7 points, with votes still being counted. The last time Democrats won the Southern popular vote was 1984 in the Senate and 1992 in the House. Analyst Nate Silver found the largest Democratic gains in the U.S. House popular vote versus 2022 came in deep-red states: Utah +29.5, North Dakota +28.6, Alabama +28.1, Indiana +24.6, Mississippi +23.7, Wyoming +23.0 and Louisiana +21.7. Utah's shift followed a successful lawsuit brought by Utah women over the state's gerrymandered maps.

House Oversight Republicans close Epstein inquiry with report clearing Trump

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

Republicans on the House Oversight Committee ended their Jeffrey Epstein inquiry with a 137-page report that offered few new findings and said investigators found no evidence linking President Trump to Epstein's sex trafficking. The report blamed police and federal prosecutors for failures that allowed Epstein to continue abusing victims after authorities began investigating him in 2005. Ranking Democrat Rep. Robert Garcia called the investigation incomplete, noting it held no public hearings, that the Justice Department continues to withhold more than 2.5 million pages, that Ghislaine Maxwell's transfer was not examined, and that Attorney General Todd Blanche has not testified. Democrats said they will resume the inquiry with public hearings when they take control next year.

Kennedy family sues to block Arlington triumphal arch

tags: politics, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

Nine members of the Kennedy family filed suit to stop the planned 250-foot arch at Arlington National Cemetery, arguing it would cast a permanent shadow over their family's graves and over the eternal flame burning for President Kennedy since 1963. VoteVets published the first report tracking the structure's shadow. The Kennedys join veterans groups, the District of Columbia and the Commonwealth of Virginia in opposing construction.

Whistleblowers allege records on Trump construction projects are being destroyed

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

House Democrats are pressing the Interior Department to preserve records on President Trump's Washington-area construction projects after whistleblowers reported document destruction ahead of January's transfer of congressional power, congressional sources told CNN. Rep. Jared Huffman, in line to chair the House Natural Resources Committee, plans to send preservation requests to Interior, other agencies and companies that donated to the projects. An Interior spokesperson called the allegations 100% false. Sources familiar with the approvals said the administration is pushing to advance the projects before Democrats take control, and the committee is weighing hearings on the proposed triumphal arch and work at East Potomac Golf Links.

Chinese military-linked university obtained blacklisted Nvidia AI chips

tags: tech, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Northwestern Polytechnical University, a Chinese institution tied to the People's Liberation Army, purchased two Nvidia H200 AI chips for about $123,000 last month through a domestic supplier, according to procurement records reported by Reuters. The school has been on the U.S. Entity List since 2001, which bars such purchases under export controls.

US envoys Witkoff and Kushner may travel to Russia

tags: politics, war
sources: @oafnation_actual

Russia's TASS news agency reported that U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner could visit Russia in the coming days, according to Reuters. TASS gave no details on timing or purpose. Both envoys had just taken part in two days of U.S., Russia and Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, the first trilateral meeting since February.

Russian ambassador to the United States dies at 66

tags: politics, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Alexander Darchiev, Russia's ambassador to the United States, has died suddenly at 66, according to Reuters. The Russian Foreign Ministry gave no cause of death, and spokeswoman Maria Zakharova said he had struggled with a chronic illness. President Vladimir Putin appointed Darchiev in March 2025 to lead a rapprochement with the Trump administration.

US gas prices fall below $4 a gallon for the first time since July

tags: markets, economy
sources: @groundnews

AAA put the national average for regular gasoline at $3.98 on Tuesday, down from $4.56 earlier this year, while diesel eased to $6.16 from $6.53 in late September. The decline follows the seasonal switch to cheaper winter-blend gasoline, which AAA says typically cuts 10 to 30 cents a gallon, and growing optimism over developments in the Middle East, with Brent crude around $91 a barrel. Regular gas remains about $1 a gallon higher than before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran in late February. GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan expects prices to keep easing into Thanksgiving, possibly reaching $3.75 a gallon.

Spain holds first general strike in 14 years over housing and wages

tags: economy, politics
sources: @groundnews

Spain's two largest unions, CCOO and UGT, began a 24-hour general strike at midnight Wednesday over wages, housing and the cost of living, less than three weeks before a Nov. 29 general election. Union representatives at Santander, BBVA, Telefonica, Carrefour, Ford and Seat signed on, and police made at least 27 arrests in the first 12 hours, mostly for public order offences such as blocking highways with burning tires, with clashes at a Madrid wholesale market leaving more than a dozen people treated after police used pepper spray. The action grew out of protests over the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from her Madrid apartment, with union leaders blaming investment funds and speculators for rising rents. One survey found just under a quarter of workers planned to strike while 36.3% opposed it.

Trump plans scorched-earth final two years as support erodes

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Donald Trump has told advisers he wants to exert maximum authority over the next two years and take a scorched-earth approach, according to Axios. The plan includes building more monuments in his own honor, pursuing political opponents and attempting to rebuild the MAGA movement. The push comes as his influence wanes following the midterms, with late-night posts on Truth Social attacking outlets including the New York Times.

Hegseth reprimanded by sentinel at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

A U.S. Army sentinel guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier in Arlington, Virginia reprimanded Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his advisers on Veterans Day, according to CNN. Hegseth was taking photographs in front of the tomb with his wife, chief of staff, deputy chief of staff and others following the Veterans Day ceremony, and some in the group were talking and laughing near the memorial. The soldier patrolling the front of the tomb called out to correct the group. Video of the exchange has since circulated.

Palantir CEO Alex Karp describes himself and his company as progressive

tags: tech, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Palantir co-founder and chief executive Alex Karp told Politico he has been a Democrat his entire life and that the company's products are essentially progressive, using the word progressive eight times to describe his philosophy. Karp, who has previously criticized the Democratic Party, said Democrats corrected course enough in 2026 to win back his support in 2028 and pointed to his far-left upbringing. The comments mark a shift for a company with extensive government contracts and close ties to the Trump administration.

Ramaswamy steps back from social media after Ohio governor loss

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Vivek Ramaswamy has updated his account on X to say it is not actively managed, following his defeat by Dr. Amy Acton in the Ohio governor's race. The change suggests a withdrawal from public political activity, at least for now.
